candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care → Case Management/Continuity of Care: provide discharge education, coordinate care across settings, facilitate referrals/follow-up, and communicate client information needed for continuity of care.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — transition planning and continuity after heart-failure hospitalization
candidate.educational_objective: Plan heart-failure transitions of care using comprehensive discharge education, symptom/weight monitoring instructions, timely follow-up, and clear communication with outpatient clinicians.

options.A: Provide clear discharge instructions on medications, weight and symptom monitoring, arrange timely follow-up, and communicate the transition plan to outpatient clinicians.
options.B: Limit discharge education to the medication list because weight monitoring and symptom-response plans are best deferred to a later outpatient visit.
options.C: Avoid early follow-up after discharge because contacting clients soon after hospitalization has no role in continuity of heart-failure care.
options.D: Use the program as a replacement for ongoing outpatient heart-failure management once the client has received discharge instructions.

candidate.rationale: The AHA/ACC/HFSA guideline recommends comprehensive transitional planning after heart-failure hospitalization. Discharge material should address medications, follow-up, weight monitoring, and what to do if symptoms worsen, and the transition plan should be communicated clearly to clinicians providing follow-up care. The guideline also identifies early outpatient follow-up as a central element of transitional care. Therefore, A is correct. B omits key discharge content, C rejects an emphasized continuity strategy, and D incorrectly substitutes a transition program for ongoing care.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Directly supports comprehensive discharge education, early follow-up, and communication of the transition plan as evidence-based heart-failure continuity-of-care strategies.
candidate.source_document_title: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure
candidate.source_locator: Hospitalized HF → transitions/discharge supportive text: written discharge instructions should address activity, diet, discharge medications, follow-up appointment, weight monitoring, cardiac rehabilitation, and what to do if symptoms worsen; the transitional plan and medication/diagnosis changes should be communicated to outpatient clinicians. Early outpatient follow-up is described as a central element of transitional care and may reduce gaps in understanding; disease-management/case-management programs may decrease rehospitalization.
candidate.source_organization: American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology/Heart Failure Society of America
candidate.stem: A hospital is designing a transition-of-care program for clients discharged after a heart-failure hospitalization. Which program component best aligns with the AHA/ACC/HFSA guideline?
